poem_stanzas:
An imaginary line that circles the middle of the world
I divide the planet into a north and a south
The sun stands overhead here at the height of noon
And the days and nights are equal all year round

Sailors cross me and mark the event with song
I am drawn on every globe in a bold black band
The heat is fierce and the rainforest grows
And I pass through Ecuador, Kenya, and Brazil
ciphers.hint: The imaginary line around the middle of the earth.

poem_stanzas:
Two imaginary lines that ring the warmer zone
Between me and my brother lies the sun's own path
Cancer and Capricorn are the names we bear
And I mark the edge of the sunburnt band

I am also a word for the turning of the sun
Where the heat is endless and the palm trees grow
I sit above the middle line and below it too
And a suntan lotion and a cocktail share my name
ciphers.hint: Either of two warm lines circling the earth near the equator.

poem_stanzas:
A line drawn from pole to pole across the globe
The sun crosses the highest of my kind at noon
I mark both a length of time and a place on the earth
And Greenwich is the famous one that starts the count

In your body I am a channel of flowing energy
On a map I am a ring that measures the east and west
China has her own and Paris had hers too
And I am the noon-day line, the crest of the day
ciphers.hint: An imaginary line running from pole to pole, or the noon high point.

poem_stanzas:
I measure how far north or south you stand
I run in flat circles parallel to the middle line
The poles are ninety of my degrees away
And I give a place its climate and its light

Sailors take me with a sextant and the stars
I am written first in the coordinates of a town
My partner measures the east and west instead
And the tropics and the polar circles lie at my marks
ciphers.hint: The distance of a place north or south of the equator.

poem_stanzas:
The high ridge where the rain decides which way to run
Every drop on my back must choose a downhill path
I divide two river valleys by a line of height
And the map is redrawn along my spine

I am also a moment when everything changes course
A turning point in history or in a life
The shed that holds the water on a farm
And the boundary between two catchments of the land
ciphers.hint: The dividing line between two river drainage areas, or a turning point.

poem_stanzas:
The gas you breathe to keep the body alive
One fifth of the air and most of the sea
Two atoms of me ride with the trees' green work
And without me a candle and a lung go dark

A hospital mask may carry me to the sick
I am named for the acid-making of the old chemists
I combine with iron to make the blood red
And rust is my slow quarrel with metal
ciphers.hint: The gas in air that living things need to breathe.

poem_stanzas:
The gas that fills most of the air you walk in
I am lazy and calm and slow to react
Plants need me but cannot take me straight from the sky
And lightning and bacteria crack me loose

I make the bubbles that keep the crisps fresh
I freeze into a fog for the doctor's probe
I am named for the salt that makes gunpowder
And I am the opposite of the one you breathe
ciphers.hint: The gas that makes up most of the air.

poem_stanzas:
The flow of a river or the rush of the sea
In a wire I am the march of tiny charges
I am also the kind you keep up to date
And a currant bun is my homophone cousin

Rapids carry me and the tide is one of mine
The news of the moment and the fashionable mode
Amp and volt together give me my push
And I run through a circuit when the switch is thrown
ciphers.hint: A flow of water, air, or electricity; the present time.

poem_stanzas:
I belong to the star at the center of our sky
A panel drinks me and turns me to power
An eclipse and a system both carry my name
And a garden lamp may glow from my stored charge

I am the opposite of the moon's adjective
I warm the roof that heats the water tank
The wind and I compete as cleaner kinds of power
And my word comes from the Latin for the sun
ciphers.hint: Relating to the sun.

poem_stanzas:
I belong to the pale orb that rules the night
A month and a calendar are shaped by my turning
An eclipse and a rover both take my name
And a landing took a small step for mankind

I tug the tides with my quiet pull
I am the opposite of the sun's adjective
The Chinese measure their new year by my phases
And a wolf is said to howl at my face
ciphers.hint: Relating to the moon.

poem_stanzas:
A paper-thin biscuit that snaps between the teeth
I come in a tube with a cream in my middle
The priest holds me as a thin disc of bread
And the microchip is built upon my kind

I am a sheet of ice cream pressed between two
Delicate, light, and gone in a single bite
A small square given with the sacrament
And I sit atop a sundae or a pudding
ciphers.hint: A very thin crisp biscuit, often served with ice cream.

poem_stanzas:
A frozen dessert with no milk at all
Fruit and sugar churned into a smooth cold heap
I follow the main course to clean the palate
And a lemon or a mango suits me best

I am colder than a cream and lighter than a cake
The Italians and the French both claim my name
A small scoop in a glass between two dishes
And I melt to syrup if you are too slow
ciphers.hint: A frozen dessert of fruit and sugar, without milk.

poem_stanzas:
An Italian ice cream, denser than the rest
Churned slowly with less air and served with a spatula
Pistachio and lemon are my famous kinds
And a wanderer in Rome licks me from a cone

I am milk, sugar, and flavor, softly frozen
My name comes from the Italian for frozen
I sit in a glass case with many colored bins
And I am smoother and richer than my cousin
ciphers.hint: A dense Italian-style ice cream.

poem_stanzas:
A crisp sweet cloud of whipped egg white and sugar
I crown a lemon pie and I float on a pudding
Bake me low and I dry into a hollow shell
And a pavlova is built upon my back

I am tricky in the damp and weep in the fridge
A torched top on a tart makes me brown
My name is French for a small sweet nothing
And I crumble to dust at the touch of a spoon
ciphers.hint: A light crisp topping of whipped egg white and sugar.

poem_stanzas:
I rise in the oven like a golden mountain
Eggs and air are the secret of my height
Open the door too soon and I collapse
And I am served the moment I come out

My name is French for blown up or puffed
Sweet or savoury, I am a delicate gamble
A ramekin is my little dish and throne
And a fallen one is a cook's quiet shame
ciphers.hint: A light baked dish that puffs up in the oven.

poem_stanzas:
Flat sheets of pasta layered in a dish
Meat and tomato and cheese between my leaves
I am baked until the top turns golden brown
And a fat cat in a comic loves me most

I am an Italian name for the pot and the food
My layers hide a white bechamel sauce
Cut me into squares and lift me with a spade
And I taste better the day after I am made
ciphers.hint: An oven-baked Italian dish of layered pasta.

poem_stanzas:
Dough made from durum and rolled into shapes
Spaghetti, penne, fusilli, and bows
I am boiled until I am tender to the bite
And the Italian word just means paste

I come in a box or fresh from a machine
I hold the sauce in the hollow of my form
A fork can twirl me round and round
And I am the base of a thousand suppers
ciphers.hint: Italian food made from a dough of flour and water.

poem_stanzas:
A snake with a triangular head and a deadly bite
My fangs fold back and my venom flows
I hiss a warning before I ever strike
And I give my name to a traitor and a car

I am not the harmless grass snake in the hedge
The adder of Britain is one of my kin
A short temper is said to be my nature
And my name means a lurking, poisonous kind
ciphers.hint: A venomous snake with a triangular head.

poem_stanzas:
A broad-winged bird that circles on the thermals
I mew above the fields and scan for prey
In America my name means a vulture instead
And I sit on a fence post hunched and patient

I am not the noble falcon of the hunt
I eat the rabbit and the worm and the road-kill
My call is a plaintive, cat-like cry
And a rude word for a coward shares my sound
ciphers.hint: A large soaring bird of prey, related to the hawk.

poem_stanzas:
A monkey with a long dog-like face
I live in a troop on the African rocks
My backside is bright and my temper is short
And I bark and yawn to show my teeth

I am bigger than a monkey and uglier than an ape
I have a mane like a lion and hands like a man
I groom my friends and I fight my rivals
And my name is also an insult for a fool
ciphers.hint: A large ground-dwelling monkey with a dog-like face.

poem_stanzas:
A slow walker armored in a thousand quills
I shuffle through the woods at night
Touch me and I fire my needles backward
And a fisher and a lion both regret the attempt

I am the largest of the spiny rodents
My quills are hair hardened into spikes
I climb a tree and eat the bark and bud
And I rattle my weapons when I am afraid
ciphers.hint: A rodent covered in sharp protective quills.

poem_stanzas:
A creature in a suit of bony plates
I roll into a ball when danger comes
I dig the earth with claws and eat the ants
And I walk the Texas roadside, armored and slow

My name is Spanish for the little armored one
I am a cousin of the sloth and the anteater
My bands let me curl up like a pinecone
And I carry my shield with me wherever I go
ciphers.hint: A burrowing animal with a bony armored shell.

poem_stanzas:
A masked bandit that raids the rubbish bin
My ringed tail and black mask mark me out
I wash my food by dunking it in water
And I climb down a tree head-first

I am a night creature of the North American woods
My clever paws open jars and latches
I look like a small burglar in a fur coat
And a famous hero of the galaxy takes my name
ciphers.hint: A night animal with a black mask and a ringed tail.

poem_stanzas:
A bundle of strings upon a long stick
I drink the water and I scrub the floor
I stand in a bucket in the corner of the kitchen
And a tangled head of hair may be called my name

I chase the dirt across the tiles
I am the sailor's chore and the cleaner's tool
Wring me out and dunk me once again
And I leave a wet trail where I have been
ciphers.hint: A tool with a long handle used for washing floors.

poem_stanzas:
A slippery bar that turns water into lather
I remove the grease and the smell of the day
I sit in a little dish by the sink
And bubbles are my cheerful signature

I am made from fat and lye in a slow reaction
I come as a bar or a squirt of liquid gel
A dirty mouth is said to deserve my taste
And I make a bathtub dangerous to step from
ciphers.hint: A substance used with water for washing and cleaning.

poem_stanzas:
A soft rectangle that dries the dampened skin
I hang upon a rail or fold upon a shelf
At the seaside I am spread upon the sand
And the hotel staff leave me folded as a swan

I come in bath and hand and tiny face sizes
My fabric is named for me and mine
I wrap the swimmer and I dry the dish
And I am thrown in the ring when a fight is done
ciphers.hint: A piece of absorbent cloth for drying.

poem_stanzas:
A sharp edge that glides across the skin
I shave the beard from a morning cheek
I have a handle and one or many blades
And a wise one applies to the simplest idea

I also mean a very close contest or cut
The barber wields me with a steady wrist
I can be electric, safety, or a straight blade
And I leave the face smooth as glass
ciphers.hint: A bladed tool used for shaving.

poem_stanzas:
A row of narrow teeth with a spine
I run through the hair and leave it neat
A rooster wears one on top of his head
And a bee builds her honey in my likeness

I untangle the knots of the morning
I can be a pocket size or a wide-toothed kind
I also mean to search a place from end to end
And I sit on the bathroom shelf beside the brush
ciphers.hint: A toothed object used to arrange the hair.

poem_stanzas:
A small round face strapped to the wrist
I hold the hours and I mark the minutes
I have a crown to wind me and a glass to guard me
And my name is also the act of staying alert

I tick in my sleep and glow in the dark
The soldier keeps me and the sailor trusts me
A wrist one and a pocket one are both mine
And to keep me means to be on the lookout
ciphers.hint: A small timepiece worn on the wrist.

poem_stanzas:
A paper pocket that carries a folded message
I have a flap and a gummed edge to seal
I wear a small square stamp in my corner
And I hold the address of the one you love

I am opened with a knife or a nervous thumb
The windows of my kind show the name within
I come in white and brown and reused sizes
And I travel the world in the postman's bag
ciphers.hint: A paper cover for a written message sent by post.

poem_stanzas:
A soft white stick that writes on a dark board
I squeak across the slate and leave a dusty line
The teacher holds me and the child draws a sun
And a limestone cliff is made of my kind

I am the mark of the sidewalk hopscotch game
I break in two and still I write
I leave white fingers and a dusty sleeve
And a billiard player rubs me on a cue
ciphers.hint: A soft white stick used for writing.

poem_stanzas:
A box with a lens and a shutter and an eye
I trap a moment and keep it still forever
I count down and I flash and I click
And the photographer hides behind my back

I can be a phone or a film or a digital kind
I store the smiles and the holidays of a life
The word obscura names my dark ancestor
And I never forget the face I have captured
ciphers.hint: A device for taking photographs.

poem_stanzas:
A box that turns invisible waves into sound
I bring the news and the music of the world
I have a dial and an aerial and a voice
And a driver sings along to what I play

I am crackling and old and warm and wooden
Satellites and telescopes look for my waves
I talk and I sing and I never need a picture
And I follow the listener into the kitchen
ciphers.hint: A device that receives broadcast sound.

poem_stanzas:
A small four-stringed instrument from Hawaii
I am held in the arm and strummed with the thumb
My name means the jumping flea in the island tongue
And I am tiny cousin to the guitar

I have a wooden body and many tunings and shapes
George Formby made a bigger cousin famous
I am easy to learn and sweet to hear
And I travel to the beach in a cloth bag
ciphers.hint: A small four-stringed Hawaiian guitar.

poem_stanzas:
A shrill note made by pushing air between the lips
A small metal tube I blow to call a dog
The referee blows me and the kettle sings me
And a train gives me a long and mournful cry

I am also the sound of a falling bomb
A windy night makes me through a crack
A wolf gives me when he sees a pretty girl
And two fingers in the mouth can make me too
ciphers.hint: A high clear sound made by forcing air through the lips or a tube.

poem_stanzas:
A story told by singing in a great hall
The fat lady is said to sing only when I end
I began in Italy with Monteverdi and his kind
And I am grand, tragic, and often in a foreign tongue

A soprano and a baritone may love and die in me
I have an overture and a curtain and a pit
A soap and a space and a house take my name
And I am the largest stage for a trained voice
ciphers.hint: A play in which the words are sung to music.

poem_stanzas:
The highest common voice of a man
I sing the hero and the lover's line
In a quartet I am the one above the deep one
And a drum and a saxophone also claim my name

I soar above the bass and below the alto
The word means holding on in Italian
Pavarotti was the most famous of my kind
And I also mean the general drift of a speech
ciphers.hint: A high adult male singing voice.

poem_stanzas:
A male voice between the high one and the low
I am deep but not the deepest of them all
I often sing the father or the villain's part
And a saxophone and a horn may bear my name

My name is Greek for heavy sounding
I sit in the middle of the male range
I am warmer than the bass and fuller than the top
And a brass instrument in the band has my pitch
ciphers.hint: A male singing voice between tenor and bass.

poem_stanzas:
Small arrows thrown at a hanging board
The bullseye is my smallest and highest score
A pub is my arena and a pint is my prize
And I start at five hundred and one, counting down

I am a game and the little feathered missiles
I stick in the board with a satisfying thud
Treble twenty is the goal of every throw
And a fast finish needs nine perfect arrows
ciphers.hint: A pub game of throwing small arrows at a board.

poem_stanzas:
A green baize table with six pockets and a cue
Colored balls and a white one and a triangle
I am the game of the crimson ball and the rest
And a clever escape leaves the opponent trapped

I demand a waistcoat and a steady hand
I am often mistaken for my cousin billiards
The perfect break is a hundred and forty-seven
And a place in trouble is named for me
ciphers.hint: A table game played with a cue and colored balls.

poem_stanzas:
A martial art of the empty hand
I came from the island of Okinawa
I break a board with a shout and a strike
And my belt shows how far I have come

My name is Japanese for open hand
I use kicks and punches and sharp blocks
My cousins are judo and taekwondo and kung fu
And a white robe is my uniform
ciphers.hint: A Japanese martial art of punches and kicks.

poem_stanzas:
Three sports chained into a single race
I swim, then I cycle, then I run
I test the body from the water to the road
And the Ironman is my longest and cruelest kind

My name is Greek for three contests
The change between my parts is called a transition
I ask for stamina, not just speed
And I finish soaked, then dusty, then sore
ciphers.hint: A race combining swimming, cycling, and running.

poem_stanzas:
The longest and strongest bone in the body
I run from the hip to the knee
A break in me is a terrible thing
And I am the thigh of the meat you eat

My name is Latin, and I am one on each side
I am a hollow tube of hard and sturdy bone
The dinosaur's great leg was made of me
And I carry the whole frame when you stand
ciphers.hint: The thigh bone, the longest bone in the body.

poem_stanzas:
The shin bone that runs beside my partner
I take the weight of the knee above the ankle
The second longest in the human frame
And I am the shin you bang on the coffee table

My name is Latin for a flute or a pipe
The footballer wears guards to keep me whole
A long bone of the lower leg is me
And I stand beside a thicker companion
ciphers.hint: The shin bone.

poem_stanzas:
A small arc of hair above the window of the eye
I keep the sweat from running into the sight
I can be raised in surprise or knit in a frown
And my plucking is a delicate art

I frame the face and give it expression
A single one can climb a very tall person's face
I move when you doubt and when you are amused
And I am a shallow ridge of skin and hair
ciphers.hint: The line of hair above the eye.

poem_stanzas:
The muscular bag where the food begins to break
I growl when empty and churn when full
Acid burns within me and folds line my wall
And I turn the meal to soup before it moves on

I am the organ that a strong meal fills
I sit below the ribs and above the gut
To have a weak one is to have no nerve
And a bad joke can turn me upside down
ciphers.hint: The organ where food is digested after swallowing.

poem_stanzas:
A creature of the night with pale skin and sharp teeth
I sleep in a coffin and fear the sun
I drink the blood of the living to stay young
And a wooden stake is my nightmare

I cannot cross the threshold unless invited
A mirror will not show my face
Count Dracula is my most famous son
And I turn to a bat when I choose
ciphers.hint: A mythical undead creature that drinks blood.

poem_stanzas:
A pale shape that lingers after death
I walk the corridors and rattle the chains
Some see me and some doubt that I exist
And I say boo to the startled living

I haunt the house where I once lived
A sheet and a hollow face are my costume
I come back to finish an unfinished thing
And a sudden cold may be my presence
ciphers.hint: The spirit of a dead person said to appear to the living.

poem_stanzas:
A towering figure of the snowy peaks
My footprints are huge and my fur is white and thick
I am the abominable creature of the mountain
And some call me the missing link of the cold

I hide in the clouds of the Himalayas
Photographs of my print have caused much talk
A cartoon boy befriends a gentle giant of my kind
And I am folklore more than bone
ciphers.hint: A legendary hairy giant said to live in the snowy mountains.

poem_stanzas:
A walking corpse that will not stay in the grave
I shuffle with arms out and a hunger for brains
A bite from me can turn a healthy friend
And I gather in a shambling, moaning crowd

Haitian magic is said to have made me first
A slow one and a fast one are both my kinds
I fill the horror film and the survival game
And I am also a person who moves like a sleepwalker
ciphers.hint: A reanimated corpse from folklore and horror films.
